prompt: Several hours after a meal, your blood glucose starts to fall. Which hormone response helps bring it back up, and how?

options.text: Insulin tells muscle cells to absorb more glucose from the blood
Adrenaline converts stored body fat directly into blood glucose in the blood itself
Insulin tells the liver to release its stored glucose
Glucagon tells the liver to break down stored glycogen and release glucose into the blood

explanation: Glucagon, released by the pancreas when blood glucose is low, acts mainly on the liver, stimulating it to break glycogen down into glucose and release it — the opposite action to insulin.
